message.reasoning_content:
Key bugs: parse_u64 sets out=0 before validating → violates "out unchanged on failure" (e.g. "12x" leaves out=0 instead of caller's value). Also overflow: out*10 wraps silently, accepts values above UINT64_MAX (e.g. "18446744073789591679" wraps) — contract violation. Also empty string accepted (returns true, out=0) — contract says nonempty only. Leading zeros allowed — fine.

Registry: get returns string_view into vector while holding lock_guard... actually lock_guard releases at end of function, so view returned after lock released — but vector push_back may reallocate/move strings while readers retain views → dangling. Also add may reallocate, invalidating existing string data → retained views dangle. Also get(i) no bounds check — out-of-range read. Also mutex doesn't protect retained views: reader holds view after get returns, writer add moves strings → dangling. Also noexcept on get? get isn't noexcept... it's fine. names[i] on vector<string> — string_view of a string that may be moved by reallocation. Also add's push_back(std::move(s)) — fine.

Also parse_u64 noexcept but overflow check needed. Also parse_u64 accepts "+"? no. Also "out unchanged" — must not assign until success.

Also Registry get returns view while lock released — that's per contract "readers may retain returned values after get returns, while writers keep calling add" → dangling string data when vector reallocates during add. Fix: store shared_ptr or copy, or return std::string by value, or use deque of allocated strings that never move (e.g. vector<unique_ptr<string>> or linked list), or document locking. Minimal fix: make names a std::vector<std::unique_ptr<std::string>> or copy out.

Also get lacks bounds check → UB for i>=size.

Also parse overflow: need check out > (UINT64_MAX - d)/10 before multiply. Also empty check.

Also parse_u64 leading zeros allowed — ok. Also "0123" fine.

Also parse_u64 sets out=0 upfront — violates unchanged-on-failure. Fix: use local temp, assign at end.

Also parse_u64 accepts nonempty ASCII digits only — empty must fail.
